records.literal_gloss: And arose Jonah to flee to Tarshish from before Yahweh; and he went down [to] Joppa and found a ship going [to] Tarshish, and he gave its fare and went down into it to go with them to Tarshish, from before Yahweh.

en.L: But Jonah arose to flee to Tarshish from before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And he went down to Joppa and found a ship about to go to Tarshish; and he gave its fare and went down into it to come with them to Tarshish, from before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: But Jonah got up to run away to Tarshish, out of the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He went down to Joppa, and there he found a ship bound for Tarshish. He paid the fare and went down into the ship to sail with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: But Jonah got up and ran away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He headed for Tarshish instead. He went down to the port of Joppa and found a ship that was going to Tarshish. He paid for the trip and went down into the ship. He wanted to sail with the crew to Tarshish, to get away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

vi.L: Nhưng Giô-na chỗi dậy để trốn đến Ta-rê-si, khỏi trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Ông đi xuống Giốp-bê và gặp một chiếc tàu sắp đi Ta-rê-si; ông trả tiền vé rồi đi xuống tàu để đi cùng họ đến Ta-rê-si, khỏi trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Nhưng Giô-na đứng dậy chạy trốn đến Ta-rê-si, lánh khỏi sự hiện diện của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Ông đi xuống Giốp-bê, tìm được một chiếc tàu sắp đi Ta-rê-si. Ông trả tiền vé và xuống tàu để cùng họ vượt biển đến Ta-rê-si, xa khỏi sự hiện diện của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Nhưng Giô-na đứng dậy và trốn khỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Ông đi về hướng Ta-rê-si. Ông xuống cảng Giốp-bê và tìm được một chiếc tàu sắp đi Ta-rê-si. Ông trả tiền đi tàu rồi xuống tàu. Ông muốn cùng các thủy thủ đi Ta-rê-si để trốn xa khỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

es.L: Pero Jonás se levantó para huir a Tarsis de delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Y bajó a Jope y halló una nave que iba a Tarsis; y pagó su pasaje y bajó a ella para ir con ellos a Tarsis, de delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Pero Jonás se levantó para huir a Tarsis, lejos de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Bajó a Jope, y allí encontró un barco que iba a Tarsis. Pagó el pasaje y bajó al barco para navegar con ellos a Tarsis, lejos de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Pero Jonás se levantó y huyó {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Se dirigió a Tarsis, en dirección contraria. Bajó al puerto de Jope y encontró un barco que iba a Tarsis. Pagó el viaje y bajó al barco. Quería navegar con la tripulación hasta Tarsis para alejarse {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Mais Jonas se leva pour fuir à Tarsis, de devant la face {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Et il descendit à Joppé et trouva un navire qui allait à Tarsis ; et il en paya le prix et descendit dedans pour aller avec eux à Tarsis, de devant la face {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Mais Jonas se leva pour s’enfuir à Tarsis, loin de la présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Il descendit à Joppé, où il trouva un navire en partance pour Tarsis. Il paya le prix du voyage et descendit dans le navire pour partir avec eux à Tarsis, loin de la présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Mais Jonas s’est levé et s’est enfui loin {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Il est parti vers Tarsis. Il est descendu au port de Joppé et il a trouvé un bateau qui allait à Tarsis. Il a payé son voyage et il est descendu dans le bateau. Il voulait partir avec les marins jusqu’à Tarsis, pour s’éloigner {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Lakini Yona akainuka ili akimbilie Tarshishi kutoka mbele ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Akashuka Yafa, akapata meli iliyokuwa ikienda Tarshishi; akalipa nauli yake, akashuka ndani yake ili aende pamoja nao Tarshishi, kutoka mbele ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Lakini Yona aliondoka ili akimbilie Tarshishi, mbali na uwepo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Alishuka mpaka Yafa, akakuta huko meli iliyokuwa ikienda Tarshishi. Akalipa nauli, akashuka ndani ya meli ili asafiri pamoja nao mpaka Tarshishi, mbali na uwepo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Lakini Yona aliondoka, akamkimbia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Badala yake alielekea Tarshishi. Alishuka mpaka bandari ya Yafa, akakuta meli iliyokuwa ikienda Tarshishi. Alilipa nauli ya safari, akashuka ndani ya meli. Alitaka kusafiri pamoja na mabaharia mpaka Tarshishi, ili amkimbie {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

ko.L: 그러나 요나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 [떠나] 다시스로 도망하려고 일어났다. 그는 욥바로 내려가서 다시스로 가는 배를 찾아내고, 그 뱃삯을 치르고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞을 떠나 그들과 함께 다시스로 가려고 그 배 안으로 내려갔다.
ko.B: 그러나 요나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞을 떠나 다시스로 달아나려고 길을 나섰다. 그는 욥바로 내려가서 다시스로 가는 배 한 척을 찾았다. 그는 뱃삯을 치르고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞을 떠나 사람들과 함께 다시스로 가려고 배 안으로 내려갔다.
ko.R: 그러나 요나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 피해 달아났다. 그는 다시스로 가려고 했다. 그는 욥바 항구로 내려가서 다시스로 가는 배를 찾았다. 그는 뱃삯을 내고 배 안으로 내려갔다. 선원들과 함께 다시스까지 가서, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게서 멀리 벗어나고 싶었던 것이다.

decisions.choice: Tarshish: a distant port far to the west; Joppa: a port on the coast of Israel
decisions.reason: Tarshish was a trading port at the far western end of the Mediterranean, from which ships brought silver, iron, tin and lead (Jeremiah 10:9; Ezekiel 27:12). It is usually placed in southern Spain, though its site is not certain. Nineveh lay far to the east by land; Jonah sets off in the opposite direction, as far as ships could take him. Joppa, modern Jaffa beside Tel Aviv, was a port on the coast of Israel (2 Chronicles 2:15).

decisions.choice: from the presence of the LORD: away from the LORD, and from standing in his service
decisions.reason: The phrase is said twice, at the start and end of the verse, to frame Jonah's flight. A prophet "stood before" the LORD as his servant (1 Kings 17:1; Jeremiah 15:19); Jonah runs from that service. He does not think he can hide from God, whom he calls the maker of the sea and the dry land (verse 9), but he will not do what he is sent to do. Cain also "went out from the presence of the LORD" (Genesis 4:16). Jonah gives his own reason in 4:2.

decisions.choice: went down: the first steps of Jonah's descent
decisions.reason: Jonah "goes down" to Joppa, "down" into the ship, "down" into the hold (verse 5), and in his prayer "down" to the roots of the mountains (2:7). The repeated verb traces his flight from God as a fall, until God brings his life "up" from the pit (2:7).

decisions.choice: paid its fare: paid for his passage
decisions.reason: The word means the hire or price of the ship. It is usually taken as Jonah's fare. Some read it as the hire of the whole ship, which would show how far he was willing to go to escape; the text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: flee (L); run away (B, R); from before (L); out of / away from the presence of (B); went down (all levels)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "went down" each time, so that the reader can follow Jonah's descent (m3). Literal says "from before the LORD", word for word; Balanced says "out of" and "away from the presence of the LORD" (m2), and "sail" for going with the ship. Readable keeps the two mentions of fleeing from the LORD, adds "instead" to show that Tarshish is not where he was sent, and says "the crew" for "them".

decisions.choice: "bajó" at every level, for each step down
decisions.reason: Jonah "goes down" to Joppa, into the ship and into its hold (1:5), and in 2:7 to the roots of the mountains. Spanish "bajar" is kept for each step so the descent can be followed.

decisions.choice: "en dirección contraria" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the English Readable says with "instead": Tarshish lay the opposite way from Nineveh.

decisions.choice: "descendre" at every level for Jonah's going down (to Joppa, into the ship, 1:5 into the hold)
decisions.reason: The English meaning decision marks "went down" as the first steps of Jonah's descent; French keeps the verb even where "monter à bord" would be the usual phrase.

decisions.choice: "đi xuống" kept at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision marks "went down" as the first step of Jonah's descent (down to Joppa, down into the ship, down into the hold, down to the sea), so Vietnamese keeps "xuống" each time, even where "lên tàu" would be the everyday phrase.

decisions.choice: "Tarshishi", "Yafa", "Ninawi"
decisions.reason: The published forms: Tarshishi as Psalm 48:8 and Isaiah, Yafa as Acts 9:36 and 2 Chronicles 2:15, Ninawi as Matthew 12:41.

decisions.choice: "akashuka" / "alishuka" at every level
decisions.reason: The verb "went down" is repeated as the first steps of Jonah's descent (to Joppa, into the ship, into its hold, 1:5, and to the roots of the mountains, 2:7), so Swahili keeps one verb, "kushuka", each time.

decisions.choice: "내려가다" for "went down" at every level; "다시스", "욥바"
decisions.reason: Jonah's descent (meaning decision) is kept in the same Korean verb at every level, as the English keeps "went down", so it links with 1:5 and 2:7. Tarshish and Joppa have their published Protestant spellings [1 Kings 10:22; Acts 9:36].

source.text: וַֽיהוָ֗ה הֵטִ֤יל רֽוּחַ־גְּדוֹלָה֙ אֶל־הַיָּ֔ם וַיְהִ֥י סַֽעַר־גָּד֖וֹל בַּיָּ֑ם וְהָ֣אֳנִיָּ֔ה חִשְּׁבָ֖ה לְהִשָּׁבֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh hurled a great wind into the sea, and there was a great storm on the sea, and the ship thought to be broken up.

en.L: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hurled a great wind onto the sea, and there was a great storm on the sea, and the ship thought it would break apart.
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hurled a great wind onto the sea, and such a great storm arose on the sea that the ship was about to break apart.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} threw a powerful wind at the sea. The storm was so violent that the ship was about to break to pieces.

vi.L: Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ném một trận gió lớn xuống biển, và có một cơn bão lớn trên biển, và chiếc tàu tưởng như sắp vỡ tan.
vi.B: Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ném một trận gió lớn xuống biển, khiến biển nổi lên một cơn bão lớn đến nỗi chiếc tàu sắp vỡ tan.
vi.R: Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} quăng một trận gió mạnh xuống biển. Cơn bão dữ dội đến nỗi chiếc tàu sắp vỡ ra từng mảnh.

es.L: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lanzó un gran viento sobre el mar, y hubo una gran tempestad en el mar, y la nave pensó que se iba a romper.
es.B: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lanzó un gran viento sobre el mar, y se levantó en el mar una tempestad tan grande que el barco estaba a punto de partirse.
es.R: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} arrojó un viento muy fuerte contra el mar. La tormenta era tan violenta que el barco estaba a punto de hacerse pedazos.

fr.L: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lança un grand vent sur la mer, et il y eut une grande tempête sur la mer, et le navire pensait se briser.
fr.B: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lança un grand vent sur la mer, et une si grande tempête s’éleva sur la mer que le navire menaçait de se briser.
fr.R: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a lancé un vent très fort sur la mer. La tempête était si violente que le bateau allait se briser.

sw.L: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akatupa upepo mkuu juu ya bahari, ikawa dhoruba kuu baharini, nayo meli ikadhani kwamba itavunjika.
sw.B: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alitupa upepo mkuu juu ya bahari, ikatokea dhoruba kuu baharini hata meli ikakaribia kuvunjika.
sw.R: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliitupia bahari upepo wenye nguvu. Dhoruba ilikuwa kali sana hata meli ikakaribia kuvunjika vipande vipande.

ko.L: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 큰 바람을 바다 위로 내던지셨다. 그러자 바다에 큰 폭풍이 일어나, 그 배가 부서지게 되었다고 [여겨질 정도였다].
ko.B: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 큰 바람을 바다 위로 내던지시니, 바다에 큰 폭풍이 일어나 배가 거의 부서지게 되었다.
ko.R: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 바다에 거센 바람을 보내셨다. 폭풍이 너무나 사나워서 배가 곧 산산조각 날 것 같았다.

decisions.choice: hurled: a verb repeated through the storm
decisions.reason: The LORD hurls the wind; the sailors hurl the cargo (verse 5); Jonah tells them to hurl him into the sea (verse 12); and they hurl him (verse 15). The same verb is used each time, and the story turns on it.

decisions.choice: the ship thought it would break apart: the ship was close to breaking up
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the ship as if it could think, a vivid way of saying that it was on the point of breaking up. The verb for "break" is used of ships wrecked at sea (1 Kings 22:49; Ezekiel 27:34).

decisions.choice: But the LORD: the LORD's name comes first, setting his action against Jonah's
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "the LORD" before the verb. Jonah fled; the LORD acts. The storm is not chance but God's answer to his flight.

decisions.choice: hurled (L, B); threw (R); great (L, B); powerful ... violent (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "hurled" each time the verb comes (m1); Readable uses "threw" each time. Literal and Balanced keep "great" for the wind and the storm, as for the city and the fish; Readable uses words that suit each noun. Literal keeps the ship that "thought"; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m2).

decisions.choice: "lanzó" (L, B); "arrojó" (R), and the same verb for the cargo (1:5) and for Jonah (1:12, 15)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats one verb for "hurl" through the storm; Spanish "lanzar" is kept at Literal and Balanced each time, "arrojar" or "echar" at Readable.

decisions.choice: "la nave pensó que se iba a romper" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of the ship "thinking"; Balanced and Readable say it was about to break apart.

decisions.choice: "lancer" for the repeated verb "hurl" (1:4, 5, 12, 15) at Literal and Balanced; Readable "lancer" for the wind and "jeter" for the cargo and Jonah
decisions.reason: The English meaning decision notes that the verb runs through the storm; "lancer" can take the wind, the cargo and Jonah alike, so Literal and Balanced keep it every time.

decisions.choice: "le navire pensait se briser"
alternatives: "le navire était sur le point de se briser"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew's picture of the ship "thinking"; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: "chiếc tàu tưởng như sắp vỡ tan"
alternatives: "chiếc tàu nghĩ rằng nó sắp vỡ"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the ship "thought"; Vietnamese "tưởng như" keeps the picture without making the ship a person, which would read as an error.

decisions.choice: "kutupa" at every level for "hurl"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats one verb for the LORD hurling the wind, the sailors hurling the cargo and Jonah being hurled into the sea (1:5, 12, 15). Swahili keeps one plain verb, "kutupa", so the repetition stays visible; the English varies "hurl" and "throw" by level.

decisions.choice: "meli ikadhani kwamba itavunjika"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of the ship "thinking" it would break up; Balanced and Readable say it was about to break apart.

decisions.choice: "내던지다" (L, B) for "hurl", in 1:4, 5, 12 and 15; R "보내다", "던지다"
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated through the storm (meaning decision): the LORD hurls the wind, the sailors hurl the cargo and then Jonah. Literal and Balanced keep one Korean verb so the chain stays visible.

decisions.choice: "그 배가 부서지게 되었다고 [여겨질 정도였다]" (L)
decisions.reason: Korean cannot naturally let the ship "think"; Literal keeps the ship as subject and brackets the words that turn the idiom into Korean.

source.text: וַיִּֽירְא֣וּ הַמַּלָּחִ֗ים וַֽיִּזְעֲקוּ֮ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־אֱלֹהָיו֒ וַיָּטִ֨לוּ אֶת־הַכֵּלִ֜ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּֽאֳנִיָּה֙ אֶל־הַיָּ֔ם לְהָקֵ֖ל מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְיוֹנָ֗ה יָרַד֙ אֶל־יַרְכְּתֵ֣י הַסְּפִינָ֔ה וַיִּשְׁכַּ֖ב וַיֵּרָדַֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And feared the sailors, and they cried out, each to his god; and they hurled the things that [were] in the ship into the sea to lighten from on them. And Jonah had gone down into [the] innermost parts of the vessel, and he had lain down and fallen into deep sleep.

en.L: And the sailors were afraid, and they cried out, each to his god; and they hurled the things that [were] in the ship into the sea to lighten [it] for them. But Jonah had gone down into the innermost parts of the vessel, and he had lain down and fallen into a deep sleep.
en.B: The sailors were terrified, and each of them cried out to his own god. They hurled the cargo into the sea to lighten their load. But Jonah had gone down into the hold of the ship, where he had lain down and fallen into a deep sleep.
en.R: The sailors were very afraid. Each one cried out to his own god for help. They threw the cargo into the sea to make the ship lighter. But Jonah had gone down below deck. He was lying there in a deep sleep.

vi.L: Các thủy thủ sợ hãi, và họ kêu cầu, mỗi người với thần của mình; và họ ném những đồ vật trong tàu xuống biển để làm nhẹ [tàu] cho họ. Còn Giô-na đã đi xuống tận phía trong cùng của tàu, nằm xuống và ngủ say.
vi.B: Các thủy thủ hoảng sợ, mỗi người kêu cầu thần của mình. Họ ném hàng hóa xuống biển cho tàu nhẹ bớt. Còn Giô-na thì đã xuống khoang tàu, nằm xuống và ngủ mê.
vi.R: Các thủy thủ rất sợ hãi. Mỗi người kêu cầu thần của mình giúp đỡ. Họ ném hàng hóa xuống biển cho tàu nhẹ hơn. Còn Giô-na đã xuống dưới khoang tàu. Ông nằm đó ngủ say như chết.

es.L: Y tuvieron miedo los marineros, y clamaron cada uno a su dios; y lanzaron al mar los objetos que [había] en la nave para aligerar[la] de su peso. Pero Jonás había bajado a lo más profundo de la embarcación, y se había acostado y se había quedado profundamente dormido.
es.B: Los marineros estaban aterrados, y cada uno clamó a su propio dios. Lanzaron la carga al mar para aligerar el peso. Pero Jonás había bajado a la bodega del barco, y allí se había acostado y se había quedado profundamente dormido.
es.R: Los marineros tenían mucho miedo. Cada uno clamó a su propio dios pidiendo ayuda. Echaron la carga al mar para que el barco pesara menos. Pero Jonás había bajado al interior del barco. Estaba acostado allí, profundamente dormido.

fr.L: Et les marins eurent peur, et ils crièrent, chacun vers son dieu ; et ils lancèrent dans la mer les objets qui [étaient] dans le navire, pour alléger [leur charge]. Mais Jonas était descendu au fond du bâtiment, et il s’était couché et s’était endormi profondément.
fr.B: Les marins furent saisis de frayeur, et chacun cria vers son propre dieu. Ils lancèrent la cargaison à la mer pour alléger leur charge. Mais Jonas était descendu dans la cale du navire ; il s’y était couché et dormait d’un profond sommeil.
fr.R: Les marins ont eu très peur. Chacun a appelé son propre dieu au secours. Ils ont jeté la cargaison à la mer pour rendre le bateau plus léger. Mais Jonas était descendu au fond du bateau. Il était couché là et il dormait profondément.

sw.L: Mabaharia wakaogopa, wakalia kila mtu kwa mungu wake; wakavitupa baharini vitu vilivyokuwa ndani ya meli ili kujipunguzia [uzito]. Lakini Yona alikuwa ameshuka mpaka sehemu za ndani kabisa za chombo, akajilaza, akapitiwa na usingizi mzito.
sw.B: Mabaharia waliogopa sana, na kila mmoja akamlilia mungu wake. Wakaitupa baharini shehena iliyokuwa melini ili kupunguza uzito. Lakini Yona alikuwa ameshuka mpaka chini kabisa ndani ya meli, akajilaza huko, akapitiwa na usingizi mzito.
sw.R: Mabaharia waliogopa sana. Kila mmoja alimlilia mungu wake amsaidie. Walitupa mizigo baharini ili meli iwe nyepesi. Lakini Yona alikuwa ameshuka chini ndani ya meli. Alikuwa amelala huko usingizi mzito.

ko.L: 그러자 선원들이 두려워하여 각자 자기 신에게 부르짖었다. 그리고 그들은 배 안에 있는 물건들을 바다로 내던져 자기들에게서 [짐을] 가볍게 하려 했다. 그러나 요나는 배의 맨 밑바닥으로 내려가서 누워 깊이 잠들어 있었다.
ko.B: 선원들은 겁에 질려 저마다 자기 신에게 부르짖었다. 그들은 배를 가볍게 하려고 배에 실은 짐을 바다로 내던졌다. 그러나 요나는 배 밑창으로 내려가 누워서 깊이 잠들어 있었다.
ko.R: 선원들은 몹시 무서웠다. 그들은 저마다 자기 신에게 살려 달라고 부르짖었다. 그리고 배를 가볍게 하려고 짐을 바다에 던졌다. 그런데 요나는 배 아래 칸으로 내려가 있었다. 그는 거기 누워 깊이 잠들어 있었다.

decisions.choice: each to his god: the sailors came from different peoples and served different gods
decisions.reason: The crew of a trading ship would be a mixed company, each man praying to the god of his own people. Their prayers set off Jonah, the one man aboard who knows the God who made the sea (verse 9), asleep.

decisions.choice: the things in the ship: the cargo and gear
decisions.reason: The word is a general one for objects, vessels and equipment. They threw overboard whatever they could to lighten the ship, cargo and tackle alike (compare Acts 27:18-19).

decisions.choice: But Jonah had gone down: what Jonah had done before the storm
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts Jonah's name first and changes the form of the verb, marking a contrast and a step back in time: while the sailors struggled, Jonah had already gone below and fallen asleep. "Gone down" continues the line of verse 3.

decisions.choice: fallen into a deep sleep: a heavy sleep, like unconsciousness
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a sleep so heavy that a person is unaware of what goes on around him (Judges 4:21; Daniel 8:18). The captain's question in verse 6 uses the same word.

decisions.choice: the things (L); the cargo (B, R); lighten [it] for them (L); lighten the load (B); the innermost parts of the vessel (L); the hold of the ship (B); below deck (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the general word and the second, rarer word for the ship, "vessel", used only here in the Bible. Balanced and Readable say "cargo" and use the familiar terms for the lower part of a ship.

decisions.choice: "los objetos" (L); "la carga" (B, R); "lo más profundo de la embarcación" (L); "la bodega del barco" (B); "el interior del barco" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the general word for the things on board and the "innermost parts" of the vessel; Balanced uses the ship's hold, Readable a plain phrase.

decisions.choice: "thần của mình"
decisions.reason: The sailors' gods are other gods; lowercase "thần" keeps them apart from "Đức Chúa Trời", which is kept for the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: "mungu wake", lowercase
decisions.reason: The sailors' gods are written with a small letter, as "his god" is in English; "Mungu" with a capital is kept for the God of Israel. The captain's "mungu wako" (1:6) is lowercase for the same reason.

source.text: וַיִּקְרַ֤ב אֵלָיו֙ רַ֣ב הַחֹבֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ מַה־לְּךָ֣ נִרְדָּ֑ם ק֚וּם קְרָ֣א אֶל־אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אוּלַ֞י יִתְעַשֵּׁ֧ת הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים לָ֖נוּ וְלֹ֥א נֹאבֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And came near to him [the] chief of the sailors and said to him, What [is] to you, sleeping? Arise, call to your god! Perhaps the god will give thought to us, and we will not perish.

en.L: And the chief of the sailors came near to him and said to him, "What [is it] with you, sleeper? Arise, call to your god! Perhaps the god will give a thought to us, and we will not perish."
en.B: The captain came to him and said, "How can you sleep? Get up, call out to your god! Perhaps that god will take notice of us, and we will not perish."
en.R: The captain went to him and said, "How can you sleep? Get up and pray to your god! Maybe your god will notice us, and we will not die."

vi.L: Viên chỉ huy các thủy thủ đến gần ông và nói với ông: "Sao vậy, hỡi người ngủ kia? Hãy chỗi dậy, kêu cầu thần của ông! Biết đâu vị thần ấy sẽ nghĩ đến chúng ta, và chúng ta sẽ không bị chết mất."
vi.B: Thuyền trưởng đến gần ông và nói: "Sao ông lại có thể ngủ được? Hãy dậy kêu cầu thần của ông đi! Biết đâu vị thần ấy sẽ đoái đến chúng ta, và chúng ta sẽ không bị chết mất."
vi.R: Thuyền trưởng đến gặp ông và nói: "Sao ông còn ngủ được? Hãy dậy cầu nguyện với thần của ông đi! Biết đâu thần của ông sẽ để ý đến chúng ta, và chúng ta khỏi chết."

es.L: Y se le acercó el jefe de los marineros y le dijo: «¿Qué [te pasa], dormilón? ¡Levántate, clama a tu dios! Quizás el dios piense en nosotros, y no pereceremos».
es.B: El capitán se le acercó y le dijo: «¿Cómo puedes dormir? ¡Levántate, clama a tu dios! Tal vez ese dios se fije en nosotros, y no pereceremos».
es.R: El capitán fue a buscarlo y le dijo: «¿Cómo puedes dormir? ¡Levántate y ora a tu dios! Tal vez tu dios se fije en nosotros y no muramos».

fr.L: Et le chef des matelots s’approcha de lui et lui dit : « Que fais-tu là, dormeur ? Lève-toi, crie vers ton dieu ! Peut-être le dieu pensera-t-il à nous, et nous ne périrons pas. »
fr.B: Le capitaine vint le trouver et lui dit : « Comment peux-tu dormir ? Lève-toi, crie vers ton dieu ! Peut-être ce dieu-là fera-t-il attention à nous, et nous ne périrons pas. »
fr.R: Le capitaine est allé le voir et lui a dit : « Comment peux-tu dormir ? Lève-toi et prie ton dieu ! Peut-être que ton dieu fera attention à nous, et nous ne mourrons pas. »

sw.L: Ndipo mkuu wa mabaharia akamkaribia, akamwambia, "Una nini, wewe mwenye usingizi? Inuka, umlilie mungu wako! Huenda mungu huyo atatukumbuka, nasi hatutaangamia."
sw.B: Nahodha alimwendea, akamwambia, "Unawezaje kulala? Inuka, umlilie mungu wako! Huenda mungu huyo atatuangalia, nasi hatutaangamia."
sw.R: Nahodha alimwendea, akamwambia, "Unawezaje kulala? Inuka umwombe mungu wako! Labda mungu wako atatuona, nasi hatutakufa."

ko.L: 그러자 뱃사람들의 우두머리가 그에게 다가와 그에게 말했다. "잠자는 사람이여, 당신에게 [무슨 일이 있습니까]? 일어나 당신의 신에게 외치십시오! 혹시 그 신이 우리를 생각해 주어서 우리가 망하지 않을지도 모릅니다."
ko.B: 선장이 그에게 와서 말했다. "어떻게 이런 때에 잠을 잘 수 있습니까? 일어나 당신의 신에게 부르짖으십시오! 혹시 그 신이 우리를 돌아보아 준다면, 우리가 망하지 않을지도 모릅니다."
ko.R: 선장이 요나에게 가서 말했다. "어떻게 잠을 잘 수가 있습니까? 일어나서 당신의 신에게 기도하십시오! 혹시 당신의 신이 우리를 보살펴 준다면, 우리가 죽지 않을지도 모릅니다."

decisions.choice: Arise, call: the captain unknowingly repeats the LORD's command
decisions.reason: The captain's words are the same two verbs the LORD spoke in verse 2, "arise ... call". The prophet who would not call out to Nineveh is now told by a foreigner to call on his God.

decisions.choice: the god: the god Jonah serves, whoever that may be
decisions.reason: The captain does not know who Jonah's god is (verse 8), and speaks of "the god" as one god among many. The same words, "the god", are used in the narrator's voice for the true God in chapter 3. Here they stand in a pagan's mouth and are taken as he means them, "that god".

decisions.choice: give a thought to us: take notice of us, have us in mind
decisions.reason: The verb is rare; it means to think about or to remember someone with favor. The king of Nineveh hopes in the same way: "Who knows? God may turn ... and we will not perish" (3:9).

decisions.choice: the chief of the sailors (L); the captain (B, R); What [is it] with you, sleeper? (L); How can you sleep? (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the title, "chief of the sailors", which means the captain. Balanced and Readable turn the question into the everyday "How can you sleep?" Balanced keeps "call out", as in verse 2 (m1); Readable says "pray". The god is lowercase at every level (m2).

decisions.choice: the captain says "tú" to Jonah; "dormilón" (L)
decisions.reason: The captain and the sailors address Jonah with "tú", as the term sheet sets; "dormilón" gives the Hebrew "sleeper" at Literal.

decisions.choice: The captain says "tu" to Jonah, and Jonah "vous" to the crew; "Que fais-tu là, dormeur ?" (L), "Comment peux-tu dormir ?" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets for Jonah and the sailors: one man addressed is "tu", the crew as a group "vous".

decisions.choice: the captain speaks to Jonah as "ông"
decisions.reason: The terms note: the captain and sailors say "ông" to Jonah, a stranger and passenger, and "chúng ta" / "chúng tôi" for themselves.

decisions.choice: "viên chỉ huy các thủy thủ" (L); "thuyền trưởng" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "chief of the sailors"; Balanced and Readable give the ordinary word, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "mkuu wa mabaharia" and "Una nini, wewe mwenye usingizi?" (L); "Nahodha" and "Unawezaje kulala?" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for the captain: Literal keeps "chief of the sailors" and the address to the sleeper, Balanced and Readable use the ordinary word for a ship's captain and a natural question. "Inuka" repeats God's command in 1:2.

decisions.choice: The captain and the sailors speak to Jonah, and Jonah to them, in 합쇼체 with "당신" (and "여러분" for the crew)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for Jonah: strangers speak 합쇼체 to each other, as in Genesis. The sailors among themselves (1:7) speak 해라체 as equals.

decisions.choice: "일어나 … 외치십시오" (L), echoing "일어나 … 외쳐라" in 1:2
decisions.reason: The captain unknowingly repeats the LORD's command (meaning decision); Literal keeps the same two verbs so the echo can be heard. Balanced and Readable say "부르짖다" and "기도하다", the natural words for prayer.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֗הוּ לְכוּ֙ וְנַפִּ֣ילָה גֽוֹרָל֔וֹת וְנֵ֣דְעָ֔ה בְּשֶׁלְּמִ֛י הָרָעָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לָ֑נוּ וַיַּפִּ֨לוּ֙ גּֽוֹרָל֔וֹת וַיִּפֹּ֥ל הַגּוֹרָ֖ל עַל־יוֹנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said, each to his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, so that we may know on whose account this evil [is] to us. And they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.

en.L: And they said, each to his fellow, "Come, and let us cast lots, so that we may know on whose account this evil [has come] to us." And they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
en.B: Then the sailors said to one another, "Come, let us cast lots to find out who is to blame for this disaster that has struck us." So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
en.R: The sailors said to one another, "Come on! Let us throw lots to find out whose fault this trouble is." So they threw lots, and the lot pointed to Jonah.

vi.L: Rồi họ nói với nhau: "Hãy đến, chúng ta hãy bắt thăm, để biết vì cớ ai mà tai họa này [đến] trên chúng ta." Họ bắt thăm, và thăm trúng nhằm Giô-na.
vi.B: Rồi các thủy thủ bảo nhau: "Nào, chúng ta hãy bắt thăm để biết ai đã gây ra tai họa này cho chúng ta." Vậy họ bắt thăm, và thăm trúng Giô-na.
vi.R: Các thủy thủ nói với nhau: "Nào! Chúng ta hãy bắt thăm để biết lỗi tại ai mà có tai họa này." Vậy họ bắt thăm, và thăm chỉ ra Giô-na.

es.L: Y dijeron cada uno a su compañero: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, y echemos suertes, para que sepamos por causa de quién [nos ha venido] este mal». Y echaron suertes, y la suerte cayó sobre Jonás.
es.B: Entonces los marineros se dijeron unos a otros: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, echemos suertes para averiguar quién tiene la culpa de esta desgracia que nos ha caído encima». Así que echaron suertes, y la suerte cayó sobre Jonás.
es.R: Los marineros se dijeron unos a otros: «¡{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}! Echemos suertes para descubrir de quién es la culpa de este problema». Así que echaron suertes, y la suerte señaló a Jonás.

fr.L: Et ils dirent, chacun à son compagnon : « Venez, jetons des sorts, afin que nous sachions à cause de qui ce mal [nous arrive]. » Et ils jetèrent des sorts, et le sort tomba sur Jonas.
fr.B: Puis les marins se dirent les uns aux autres : « Venez, tirons au sort pour savoir qui est responsable de ce désastre qui nous frappe. » Ils tirèrent au sort, et le sort tomba sur Jonas.
fr.R: Les marins se sont dit les uns aux autres : « Allez ! Tirons au sort pour savoir qui est la cause de ce malheur. » Ils ont tiré au sort, et le sort a désigné Jonas.

sw.L: Wakaambiana kila mtu na mwenzake, "Njooni, na tupige kura, ili tujue ni kwa sababu ya nani ubaya huu [umetupata]." Wakapiga kura, nayo kura ikamwangukia Yona.
sw.B: Kisha mabaharia wakaambiana, "Njooni, tupige kura tujue ni nani aliyetuletea maafa haya." Wakapiga kura, nayo kura ikamwangukia Yona.
sw.R: Mabaharia waliambiana, "Njooni! Tupige kura tujue taabu hii ni kosa la nani." Basi wakapiga kura, nayo kura ikamwonyesha Yona.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 서로에게 말했다. "자, 제비를 뽑아서, 누구 때문에 이 악한 일이 우리에게 [닥쳤는지] 알아보자." 그들이 제비를 뽑으니, 제비가 요나에게 떨어졌다.
ko.B: 그때 선원들이 서로 말했다. "자, 제비를 뽑아서 누구 때문에 이 재앙이 우리에게 닥쳤는지 알아보자." 그들이 제비를 뽑으니 요나가 걸렸다.
ko.R: 선원들이 서로 말했다. "자, 제비를 뽑아서 이 고생이 누구 탓인지 알아보자." 그래서 그들이 제비를 뽑았더니, 요나가 뽑혔다.

decisions.choice: cast lots: a way of asking God to decide
decisions.reason: Lots were marked stones or sticks drawn or thrown to reach a decision. People believed that the outcome was in God's hands (Proverbs 16:33), and Israel used lots to find a guilty person (Joshua 7:14-18; 1 Samuel 14:41-42). The sailors assume that the storm is the anger of a god at someone on board.

decisions.choice: this evil: this disaster
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for Nineveh's evil in verse 2 (see the note there). Here it means the disaster that has struck the ship.

decisions.choice: evil (L); disaster (B); trouble (R); on whose account (L); who is to blame (B); whose fault (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "evil" so that the reader can see the word recur; Balanced and Readable give its sense here (m2). "The sailors" is supplied at Balanced and Readable to show who speaks.

decisions.choice: "{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}" among the sailors
decisions.reason: The sailors speak to one another as a group, so the plural "you" takes the plural_you setting (Latin American "ustedes" by default).

decisions.choice: "este mal" (L); "esta desgracia" (B); "este problema" (R)
decisions.reason: One Hebrew word means both evil and disaster in Jonah; Literal keeps "mal" so the book's repeated word can be seen.

decisions.choice: "tai họa" at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "this evil" as "this disaster"; "điều ác" would suggest wrongdoing, so even Literal says "tai họa".

decisions.choice: "이 악한 일" (L); "이 재앙" (B); "이 고생" (R)
decisions.reason: The word is the book's "evil" (1:2), here meaning disaster (meaning decision). Literal keeps "악" in the phrase so the key word stays visible; Balanced and Readable say what it is.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו הַגִּידָה־נָּ֣א לָ֔נוּ בַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר לְמִי־הָרָעָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לָ֑נוּ מַה־מְּלַאכְתְּךָ֙ וּמֵאַ֣יִן תָּב֔וֹא מָ֣ה אַרְצֶ֔ךָ וְאֵֽי־מִזֶּ֥ה עַ֖ם אָֽתָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, Tell us, please, on whose account this evil [is] to us; what [is] your occupation, and from where do you come; what [is] your land, and from which people [are] you?

en.L: And they said to him, "Tell us, please, on whose account this evil [has come] to us. What [is] your occupation, and from where do you come? What [is] your land, and from which people [are] you?"
en.B: So they said to him, "Tell us, who is to blame for this disaster that has come on us? What is your work? Where do you come from? What is your country? What people do you belong to?"
en.R: So they asked him, "Tell us, whose fault is this trouble? What work do you do? Where do you come from? What country are you from? Who are your people?"

vi.L: Họ nói với ông: "Xin hãy nói cho chúng tôi biết, vì cớ ai mà tai họa này [đến] trên chúng tôi. Nghề của ông [là] gì, và ông từ đâu đến? Xứ của ông [là] xứ nào, và ông thuộc dân tộc nào?"
vi.B: Vậy họ nói với ông: "Hãy cho chúng tôi biết, ai đã gây ra tai họa này cho chúng tôi? Ông làm nghề gì? Ông từ đâu đến? Quê ông ở đâu? Ông thuộc dân tộc nào?"
vi.R: Vậy họ hỏi ông: "Hãy nói cho chúng tôi biết, tai họa này là lỗi tại ai? Ông làm nghề gì? Ông từ đâu đến? Ông là người nước nào? Dân tộc của ông là ai?"

es.L: Y le dijeron: «Decláranos, por favor, por causa de quién [nos ha venido] este mal. ¿Cuál [es] tu oficio, y de dónde vienes? ¿Cuál [es] tu tierra, y de qué pueblo [eres] tú?».
es.B: Entonces le dijeron: «Dinos, ¿quién tiene la culpa de esta desgracia que nos ha caído encima? ¿En qué trabajas? ¿De dónde vienes? ¿Cuál es tu país? ¿A qué pueblo perteneces?».
es.R: Entonces le preguntaron: «Dinos, ¿de quién es la culpa de este problema? ¿En qué trabajas? ¿De dónde vienes? ¿De qué país eres? ¿Quién es tu gente?».

fr.L: Et ils lui dirent : « Fais-nous donc savoir, à cause de qui ce mal [nous arrive]. Quel [est] ton métier, et d’où viens-tu ? Quel [est] ton pays, et de quel peuple [es]-tu ? »
fr.B: Alors ils lui dirent : « Dis-nous, qui est responsable de ce désastre qui nous arrive ? Quel est ton travail ? D’où viens-tu ? Quel est ton pays ? De quel peuple es-tu ? »
fr.R: Alors ils lui ont demandé : « Dis-nous, qui est la cause de ce malheur ? Quel travail fais-tu ? D’où viens-tu ? De quel pays es-tu ? Qui est ton peuple ? »

sw.L: Wakamwambia, "Tafadhali tuambie, ni kwa sababu ya nani ubaya huu [umetupata]? Kazi yako [ni] nini, nawe unatoka wapi? Nchi yako [ni] ipi, nawe [u] wa watu gani?"
sw.B: Basi wakamwambia, "Tuambie, ni nani aliyesababisha maafa haya yaliyotupata? Kazi yako ni nini? Unatoka wapi? Nchi yako ni ipi? Wewe ni wa taifa gani?"
sw.R: Basi wakamwuliza, "Tuambie, taabu hii ni kosa la nani? Unafanya kazi gani? Unatoka wapi? Nchi yako ni ipi? Watu wako ni akina nani?"

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 그에게 말했다. "누구 때문에 이 악한 일이 우리에게 [닥쳤는지] 제발 우리에게 말해 주십시오. 당신의 직업은 무엇이며, 당신은 어디에서 왔습니까? 당신의 나라는 어디이며, 당신은 어느 민족입니까?"
ko.B: 그래서 그들이 그에게 말했다. "말해 주십시오. 누구 때문에 이 재앙이 우리에게 닥쳤습니까? 당신은 무슨 일을 합니까? 어디에서 왔습니까? 당신의 나라는 어디입니까? 어느 민족 사람입니까?"
ko.R: 그래서 그들이 요나에게 물었다. "말해 보십시오. 이 고생이 누구 탓입니까? 당신은 무슨 일을 하는 사람입니까? 어디에서 왔습니까? 어느 나라 사람입니까? 당신의 백성은 누구입니까?"

decisions.choice: the question "on whose account this evil has come to us" is part of the text
decisions.reason: The lot has already fallen on Jonah, yet the sailors ask again who is to blame. Some Hebrew manuscripts and some copies of the Greek translation leave this first question out. The Hebrew text is followed: the sailors want to hear it from Jonah himself before they act. This description of the manuscripts is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: a rush of questions: the sailors' fear and haste
decisions.reason: Four questions follow in a breath: his work, where he has come from, his country and his people. Jonah answers only the last, and in doing so answers the first (verse 9).

decisions.choice: occupation (L); work (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means a person's business or trade. Balanced and Readable say "work". Every level keeps the questions as questions; Balanced and Readable give each its own sentence.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עִבְרִ֣י אָנֹ֑כִי וְאֶת־יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ אֲנִ֣י יָרֵ֔א אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה אֶת־הַיָּ֖ם וְאֶת־הַיַּבָּשָֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, A Hebrew I [am], and Yahweh, [the] God of the heavens, I fear, who made the sea and the dry land.

en.L: And he said to them, "I [am] a Hebrew, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the heavens, I fear, who made the sea and the dry land."
en.B: He answered them, "I am a Hebrew, and I fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land."
en.R: Jonah answered, "I am a Hebrew. I worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of heaven. He made the sea and the land."

vi.L: Ông nói với họ: "Tôi [là] người Hê-bơ-rơ, và tôi kính sợ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của các tầng trời, Đấng đã làm nên biển và đất khô."
vi.B: Ông trả lời họ: "Tôi là người Hê-bơ-rơ. Tôi kính sợ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời trên trời, Đấng đã dựng nên biển và đất liền."
vi.R: Giô-na trả lời: "Tôi là người Hê-bơ-rơ. Tôi thờ phượng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời trên trời. Ngài đã dựng nên biển và đất."

es.L: Y les dijo: «Hebreo [soy] yo, y {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios de los cielos, temo yo, el que hizo el mar y la tierra seca».
es.B: Él les respondió: «Soy hebreo, y temo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios de los cielos, que hizo el mar y la tierra firme».
es.R: Jonás respondió: «Soy hebreo. Adoro {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios del cielo. Él hizo el mar y la tierra».

fr.L: Et il leur dit : « Je [suis] Hébreu, et je crains {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu des cieux, qui a fait la mer et la terre sèche. »
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « Je suis Hébreu, et je crains {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu des cieux, qui a fait la mer et la terre ferme. »
fr.R: Jonas leur a répondu : « Je suis Hébreu. J’adore {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu du ciel. Il a fait la mer et la terre. »

sw.L: Akawaambia, "Mimi [ni] Mwebrania, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mbinguni, ninamcha, aliyeumba bahari na nchi kavu."
sw.B: Akawajibu, "Mimi ni Mwebrania, nami ninamcha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mbinguni, aliyeumba bahari na nchi kavu."
sw.R: Yona akawajibu, "Mimi ni Mwebrania. Ninamwabudu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mbinguni. Yeye ndiye aliyeumba bahari na nchi kavu."

ko.L: 그가 그들에게 말했다. "저는 히브리 사람이고, 바다와 마른 땅을 만드신 하늘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 두려워합니다."
ko.B: 요나가 그들에게 대답했다. "저는 히브리 사람입니다. 저는 바다와 육지를 만드신 하늘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 경외합니다."
ko.R: 요나가 대답했다. "저는 히브리 사람입니다. 저는 하늘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬깁니다. 그분께서 바다와 땅을 만드셨습니다."

decisions.choice: a Hebrew: the name an Israelite gave himself before foreigners
decisions.reason: In the Bible, "Hebrew" is used mostly where Israelites speak with or are named by other peoples (Genesis 14:13; 40:15; Exodus 2:6-7; 1 Samuel 4:6). Jonah tells the sailors which people he belongs to.

decisions.choice: I fear the LORD: I worship and revere the LORD
decisions.reason: To "fear" the LORD is to stand in awe of him and serve him (Deuteronomy 10:12). The word is a key to the chapter: the sailors were afraid (verse 5), are filled with great fear at Jonah's words (verse 10), and end by fearing the LORD (verse 16). Jonah says he fears the LORD while running from him.

decisions.choice: the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land: the LORD rules the very sea Jonah is fleeing on
decisions.reason: "The God of heaven" is a title Israelites used before foreigners (Genesis 24:7; Ezra 1:2; Daniel 2:18). By naming the LORD as maker of the sea and the dry land, Jonah tells the sailors that the storm comes from his God, and shows that he cannot escape him. The "dry land" returns when the sailors try to reach it (verse 13) and when the fish puts Jonah out on it (2:11).

decisions.choice: fear (L, B); worship (R); heavens (L); heaven (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "fear" so that the reader can follow the word through the chapter (m2); Readable says "worship", which is what Jonah means. Literal keeps the plural "heavens" of the Hebrew; Balanced and Readable use the familiar title "the God of heaven".

decisions.choice: "temo" (L, B); "Adoro" (R); "el Dios de los cielos" (L, B); "el Dios del cielo" (R)
decisions.reason: "El Dios de los cielos" is the Spanish of Ezra and 2 Chronicles 36:23; Readable says what fearing the LORD means here, worship.

decisions.choice: "le Dieu des cieux" (L, B), "le Dieu du ciel" (R)
alternatives: "le Dieu du ciel" at every level
decisions.reason: As Ezra and Daniel in the published French and the term sheet.

decisions.choice: Literal puts the verb first ("je crains le SEIGNEUR")
alternatives: "et le SEIGNEUR ..., c'est lui que je crains"
decisions.reason: French cannot put the object before the verb without a cleft sentence, which would be heavier than the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "Đức Chúa Trời của các tầng trời" (L); "Đức Chúa Trời trên trời" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The terms note gives "Đức Chúa Trời trên trời" for "the God of heaven"; Literal keeps the Hebrew plural "heavens", as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: "tôi kính sợ CHÚA" with the verb before its object
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "the LORD" first for weight; a fronted object in Vietnamese would need "thì" and break the long apposition, so even Literal uses the normal order.

decisions.choice: "Mungu wa mbinguni"
decisions.reason: As Ezra and the term sheet for these books. The Hebrew plural "heavens" is ordinary Swahili "mbinguni" at every level.

decisions.choice: "두려워합니다" (L); "경외합니다" (B); "섬깁니다" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "두려워하다" so that Jonah's "I fear the LORD" stays linked to the sailors' fear in 1:5, 10 and 16. Balanced says "경외하다", the published word for reverent fear of God; Readable says what the fear means in practice, as the English "worship".

decisions.choice: "히브리 사람"; "하늘의 하나님"
decisions.reason: The published forms [Gen 14:13; Ezra 1:2]: "하늘의 하나님" for "the God of the heavens", with the plural left out at every level, since Korean "하늘" already covers it.

source.text: וַיִּֽירְא֤וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ יִרְאָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו מַה־זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֑יתָ כִּֽי־יָדְע֣וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים כִּֽי־מִלִּפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ ה֣וּא בֹרֵ֔חַ כִּ֥י הִגִּ֖יד לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And feared the men a fear great, and they said to him, What [is] this you have done? For knew the men that from before Yahweh he [was] fleeing, for he had told them.

en.L: And the men feared a great fear, and they said to him, "What [is] this you have done?" For the men knew that from the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} he was fleeing, for he had told them.
en.B: Then the men were seized with great fear, and they said to him, "What is this that you have done?" For the men knew that he was running away from the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because he had told them.
en.R: Then the sailors were terrified. "What have you done?" they asked him. They knew that Jonah was running away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because he had told them.

vi.L: Những người ấy sợ hãi một nỗi sợ lớn, và họ nói với ông: "Ông đã làm gì [thế này]?" Vì những người ấy biết rằng ông đang trốn khỏi trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vì ông đã nói cho họ biết.
vi.B: Những người ấy vô cùng sợ hãi và nói với ông: "Ông đã làm gì thế này?" Vì họ biết ông đang chạy trốn khỏi sự hiện diện của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, bởi ông đã nói cho họ biết.
vi.R: Các thủy thủ hết sức kinh hãi. Họ hỏi ông: "Ông đã làm gì vậy?" Họ biết Giô-na đang trốn khỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vì ông đã kể cho họ nghe.

es.L: Y temieron los hombres con gran temor, y le dijeron: «¿Qué [es] esto que has hecho?». Porque sabían los hombres que de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} él huía, porque se lo había contado.
es.B: Entonces los hombres se llenaron de un gran temor, y le dijeron: «¿Qué es esto que has hecho?». Porque los hombres sabían que él huía de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, ya que él se lo había contado.
es.R: Entonces los marineros se aterrorizaron. «¿Qué has hecho?», le preguntaron. Sabían que Jonás estaba huyendo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, porque él se lo había contado.

fr.L: Et les hommes craignirent [avec] une grande crainte, et ils lui dirent : « Qu’est-ce que cela, que tu as fait ? » Car les hommes savaient que de devant la face {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} il fuyait, car il le leur avait raconté.
fr.B: Alors les hommes furent saisis d’une grande crainte, et ils lui dirent : « Qu’as-tu donc fait ? » Car ces hommes savaient qu’il fuyait loin de la présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, parce qu’il le leur avait dit.
fr.R: Alors les marins ont été terrifiés. « Qu’est-ce que tu as fait ? » lui ont-ils demandé. Ils savaient que Jonas fuyait loin {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, parce qu’il le leur avait dit.

sw.L: Watu wale wakaogopa kwa hofu kuu, wakamwambia, "Ni nini hiki ulichofanya?" Kwa maana watu wale walijua kwamba alikuwa akikimbia kutoka mbele ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa sababu alikuwa amewaambia.
sw.B: Ndipo watu wale wakashikwa na hofu kuu, wakamwambia, "Ni nini hiki ulichofanya?" Kwa maana walijua kwamba alikuwa akikimbia mbali na uwepo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa sababu alikuwa amewaambia.
sw.R: Mabaharia waliogopa sana. Wakamwuliza, "Umefanya nini?" Walijua kwamba Yona alikuwa akimkimbia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa sababu alikuwa amewaambia.

ko.L: 그러자 그 사람들이 큰 두려움으로 두려워하며 그에게 말했다. "당신이 어찌하여 이런 일을 했습니까?" 그 사람들은 그가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 도망하고 있다는 것을 알았으니, 그가 그들에게 말했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러자 그 사람들은 몹시 두려워하며 그에게 말했다. "당신이 어쩌자고 이런 일을 했습니까?" 그들은 요나가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞을 떠나 달아나는 중이라는 것을 알고 있었다. 요나가 그들에게 말해 주었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그러자 선원들은 겁에 질렸다. "당신은 도대체 무슨 일을 저질렀습니까?" 그들이 요나에게 물었다. 그들은 요나가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 피해 달아나고 있다는 것을 알고 있었다. 요나가 그들에게 이야기했기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: What is this you have done? A cry of horror more than a question
decisions.reason: The same words are spoken to Eve in Genesis 3:13. The sailors do not need an answer; they are appalled that a man would run from the God who made the sea.

decisions.choice: for the men knew ... because he had told them: the narrator explains
decisions.reason: The story has not said that Jonah told the sailors he was fleeing; the narrator adds it here. Jonah must have told them, earlier or now, as part of his answer in verse 9.

decisions.choice: feared a great fear: were filled with great fear
decisions.reason: Hebrew often strengthens a verb with a noun of the same root. Their fear grows from verse 5 to here, and in verse 16 the same words describe their fear of the LORD.

decisions.choice: feared a great fear (L); were seized with great fear (B); were terrified (R); the men (L, B); the sailors (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew pattern; Balanced keeps "great fear" with a natural verb; Readable says "terrified". The Hebrew calls them "the men" from here on; Readable keeps "the sailors" so that young readers know who is meant.

decisions.choice: "temieron ... con gran temor" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew repetition of verb and noun; Balanced "se llenaron de un gran temor", Readable "se aterrorizaron".

decisions.choice: "sợ hãi một nỗi sợ lớn"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew's cognate repetition, which Vietnamese can say; Balanced and Readable give the sense.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ מַה־נַּ֣עֲשֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ וְיִשְׁתֹּ֥ק הַיָּ֖ם מֵֽעָלֵ֑ינוּ כִּ֥י הַיָּ֖ם הוֹלֵ֥ךְ וְסֹעֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, What shall we do to you, so that may be quiet the sea from on us? For the sea [was] going and storming.

en.L: And they said to him, "What shall we do to you, so that the sea may become quiet for us?" For the sea was growing more and more stormy.
en.B: So they asked him, "What should we do to you to make the sea calm down for us?" For the sea was getting rougher and rougher.
en.R: The storm was getting worse and worse. So they asked Jonah, "What should we do to you to make the sea calm down?"

vi.L: Họ nói với ông: "Chúng tôi phải làm gì với ông, để biển lặng xuống cho chúng tôi?" Vì biển càng lúc càng động dữ.
vi.B: Vậy họ hỏi ông: "Chúng tôi phải làm gì với ông để biển lặng lại cho chúng tôi?" Vì sóng biển càng lúc càng dữ dội.
vi.R: Bão biển mỗi lúc một dữ hơn. Vậy họ hỏi Giô-na: "Chúng tôi phải làm gì với ông để biển lặng lại?"

es.L: Y le dijeron: «¿Qué te haremos para que el mar se nos calme?». Porque el mar se iba embraveciendo cada vez más.
es.B: Así que le preguntaron: «¿Qué debemos hacer contigo para que el mar se nos calme?». Porque el mar se encrespaba cada vez más.
es.R: La tormenta empeoraba cada vez más. Así que le preguntaron a Jonás: «¿Qué debemos hacer contigo para que el mar se calme?».

fr.L: Et ils lui dirent : « Que te ferons-nous, pour que la mer se calme pour nous ? » Car la mer allait en se déchaînant.
fr.B: Ils lui demandèrent donc : « Que devons-nous te faire pour que la mer se calme autour de nous ? » Car la mer devenait de plus en plus agitée.
fr.R: La tempête devenait de plus en plus violente. Alors les marins ont demandé à Jonas : « Qu’est-ce que nous devons te faire pour que la mer se calme ? »

sw.L: Wakamwambia, "Tukutendee nini, ili bahari itutulie?" Kwa maana bahari ilikuwa ikizidi kuchafuka.
sw.B: Basi wakamwuliza, "Tukufanye nini ili bahari itutulie?" Kwa maana bahari ilikuwa ikizidi kuchafuka zaidi na zaidi.
sw.R: Dhoruba ilikuwa ikizidi kuwa kali. Kwa hiyo wakamwuliza Yona, "Tukufanye nini ili bahari itulie?"

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 그에게 말했다. "우리가 당신을 어떻게 해야 바다가 우리에게서 잔잔해지겠습니까?" 바다가 점점 더 거칠어지고 있었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그래서 그들이 그에게 물었다. "우리가 당신을 어떻게 해야 바다가 잔잔해지겠습니까?" 바다가 점점 더 사나워지고 있었다.
ko.R: 폭풍은 점점 더 심해졌다. 그래서 선원들이 요나에게 물었다. "우리가 당신을 어떻게 해야 바다가 잠잠해지겠습니까?"

decisions.choice: the sea was going and storming: the storm was growing worse and worse
decisions.reason: The verb "go" joined to another verb means that something keeps on and increases (Genesis 26:13; 2 Samuel 3:1). The sea was getting steadily rougher.

decisions.choice: What shall we do to you? The sailors ask the LORD's prophet what his God requires
decisions.reason: Jonah has told them that the storm comes from the LORD. The sailors do not act on their own; they ask the man who knows this God what must be done.

decisions.choice: the storm was getting worse and worse, first (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives the reason last. Readable puts it first, so that the question follows from it, and says "the storm" for the sea that kept storming.

decisions.choice: "se iba embraveciendo cada vez más" (L)
decisions.reason: Spanish "ir" with a gerund gives the Hebrew "going and storming", a storm that keeps growing, without adding words.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם שָׂא֨וּנִי֙ וַהֲטִילֻ֣נִי אֶל־הַיָּ֔ם וְיִשְׁתֹּ֥ק הַיָּ֖ם מֵֽעֲלֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֚י יוֹדֵ֣עַ אָ֔נִי כִּ֣י בְשֶׁלִּ֔י הַסַּ֧עַר הַגָּד֛וֹל הַזֶּ֖ה עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Pick me up and hurl me into the sea, and will be quiet the sea from on you; for knowing I [am] that on my account this great storm [is] on you.

en.L: And he said to them, "Pick me up and hurl me into the sea, and the sea will become quiet for you; for I know that on my account this great storm [has come] upon you."
en.B: He answered them, "Pick me up and hurl me into the sea, and the sea will calm down for you. For I know that it is my fault that this great storm has come upon you."
en.R: "Pick me up and throw me into the sea," Jonah answered. "Then the sea will calm down. I know that this terrible storm has come on you because of me."

vi.L: Ông nói với họ: "Hãy nhấc tôi lên và ném tôi xuống biển, thì biển sẽ lặng xuống cho các ông; vì tôi biết rằng vì cớ tôi mà cơn bão lớn này [đã đến] trên các ông."
vi.B: Ông trả lời họ: "Hãy khiêng tôi lên và ném xuống biển, thì biển sẽ lặng lại cho các ông. Vì tôi biết chính tôi là nguyên nhân khiến cơn bão lớn này ập đến trên các ông."
vi.R: Giô-na trả lời: "Hãy khiêng tôi lên và quăng xuống biển. Khi đó biển sẽ lặng lại. Tôi biết cơn bão khủng khiếp này đến với các ông là vì tôi."

es.L: Y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Tómenme|Tomadme}} y {{plural_you:láncenme|lanzadme}} al mar, y el mar se {{plural_you:les|os}} calmará; porque yo sé que por mi causa [ha venido] sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} esta gran tempestad».
es.B: Él les respondió: «{{plural_you:Tómenme|Tomadme}} y {{plural_you:láncenme|lanzadme}} al mar, y el mar se {{plural_you:les|os}} calmará. Porque yo sé que por mi culpa {{plural_you:les|os}} ha caído encima esta gran tempestad».
es.R: «{{plural_you:Tómenme|Tomadme}} y {{plural_you:échenme|echadme}} al mar», respondió Jonás. «Entonces el mar se calmará. Yo sé que por mi culpa {{plural_you:les|os}} ha caído encima esta terrible tormenta».

fr.L: Et il leur dit : « Prenez-moi et lancez-moi dans la mer, et la mer se calmera pour vous ; car je sais, moi, que c’est à cause de moi que cette grande tempête [est] sur vous. »
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « Prenez-moi et lancez-moi dans la mer, et la mer se calmera autour de vous. Car je sais que c’est par ma faute que cette grande tempête s’est abattue sur vous. »
fr.R: « Prenez-moi et jetez-moi dans la mer, leur a répondu Jonas. Alors la mer se calmera. Je sais que c’est à cause de moi que cette terrible tempête vous est arrivée. »

sw.L: Akawaambia, "Niinueni, mnitupe baharini, nayo bahari itawatulia; kwa maana ninajua kwamba ni kwa sababu yangu dhoruba hii kuu [imewajia] juu yenu."
sw.B: Akawajibu, "Niinueni, mnitupe baharini, nayo bahari itawatulia. Kwa maana ninajua kwamba ni kosa langu kwamba dhoruba hii kuu imewajia."
sw.R: Yona akawajibu, "Niinueni mnitupe baharini. Ndipo bahari itatulia. Ninajua kwamba dhoruba hii mbaya imewapata kwa sababu yangu."

ko.L: 그가 그들에게 말했다. "저를 들어서 바다에 내던지십시오. 그러면 바다가 여러분에게서 잔잔해질 것입니다. 이 큰 폭풍이 저 때문에 여러분에게 [닥쳤다는] 것을 제가 압니다."
ko.B: 요나가 그들에게 대답했다. "저를 들어서 바다에 내던지십시오. 그러면 바다가 잔잔해질 것입니다. 이 큰 폭풍이 여러분에게 닥친 것은 저 때문이라는 것을 제가 압니다."
ko.R: "저를 들어서 바다에 던지십시오." 요나가 대답했다. "그러면 바다가 잠잠해질 것입니다. 이 무서운 폭풍이 여러분에게 닥친 것은 저 때문입니다. 저는 그것을 압니다."

decisions.choice: Jonah admits his guilt and offers his life for the sailors
decisions.reason: Jonah accepts that the storm is his fault. The text does not say why he asks to be thrown overboard instead of turning back to obey: whether to spare the sailors, to accept God's judgment, or because he would rather die than go to Nineveh (compare 4:3, 8). It records his words without explaining them.

decisions.choice: hurl (L, B); throw (R); great (L, B); terrible (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, Literal and Balanced keep "hurl" and "great", and Readable says "throw". Readable puts "Jonah answered" inside the quotation, as speech is often written.

decisions.choice: Jonah speaks to the sailors with plural_you: "{{plural_you:Tómenme|Tomadme}} y {{plural_you:láncenme|lanzadme}}" (L, B), "... {{plural_you:échenme|echadme}}" (R)
decisions.reason: Jonah answers the whole crew, so every plural "you" is a plural_you span, as the term sheet sets for this verse.

decisions.choice: Jonah says "tôi" and calls the sailors "các ông"
decisions.reason: The terms note's address for Jonah and the sailors: mutual respect between strangers.

decisions.choice: "Niinueni, mnitupe" (plural)
decisions.reason: Jonah speaks to the sailors as "ninyi", while they speak to him as "wewe" (term sheet). Swahili marks the plural in the verb, so no setting is needed.

source.text: וַיַּחְתְּר֣וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים לְהָשִׁ֛יב אֶל־הַיַּבָּשָׁ֖ה וְלֹ֣א יָכֹ֑לוּ כִּ֣י הַיָּ֔ם הוֹלֵ֥ךְ וְסֹעֵ֖ר עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And dug the men to return to the dry land, and not they were able, for the sea [was] going and storming against them.

en.L: And the men dug [in their oars] to return to the dry land, but they were not able, for the sea was growing more and more stormy against them.
en.B: Instead, the men rowed hard to bring the ship back to dry land, but they were unable to, because the sea grew rougher and rougher against them.
en.R: Instead, the sailors rowed hard to get the ship back to land. But they could not do it, because the storm kept getting worse.

vi.L: Những người ấy ra sức chèo [mạnh] để quay trở lại đất khô, nhưng họ không thể, vì biển càng lúc càng động dữ nghịch lại họ.
vi.B: Thay vào đó, những người ấy ra sức chèo để đưa tàu trở vào đất liền, nhưng không được, vì sóng biển càng lúc càng nổi dữ dội nghịch lại họ.
vi.R: Thay vì làm theo lời ông, các thủy thủ ra sức chèo để đưa tàu vào bờ. Nhưng họ không làm được, vì bão cứ càng lúc càng dữ hơn.

es.L: Y los hombres cavaron [con los remos] para volver a la tierra seca, pero no pudieron, porque el mar se iba embraveciendo cada vez más contra ellos.
es.B: Pero los hombres, en lugar de eso, remaron con fuerza para hacer volver el barco a tierra firme, y no pudieron, porque el mar se encrespaba cada vez más contra ellos.
es.R: En vez de hacerlo, los marineros remaron con todas sus fuerzas para llevar el barco de vuelta a tierra. Pero no lo lograron, porque la tormenta seguía empeorando.

fr.L: Et les hommes forcèrent [sur les rames] pour revenir à la terre sèche, mais ils ne le purent pas, car la mer allait en se déchaînant contre eux.
fr.B: Au contraire, les hommes ramèrent avec force pour ramener le navire à la terre ferme, mais ils n’y parvinrent pas, car la mer se déchaînait de plus en plus contre eux.
fr.R: Mais les marins ont ramé de toutes leurs forces pour ramener le bateau vers la terre. Ils n’ont pas réussi, parce que la tempête devenait toujours plus violente.

sw.L: Lakini watu wale wakachimba [maji kwa makasia] ili kurudi nchi kavu, wala hawakuweza, kwa maana bahari ilikuwa ikizidi kuchafuka juu yao.
sw.B: Badala yake, watu wale walipiga makasia kwa nguvu ili kuirudisha meli nchi kavu, lakini hawakuweza, kwa sababu bahari ilizidi kuchafuka dhidi yao.
sw.R: Badala yake, mabaharia walipiga makasia kwa nguvu sana ili kuifikisha meli nchi kavu. Lakini hawakuweza, kwa sababu dhoruba iliendelea kuzidi.

ko.L: 그러나 그 사람들은 마른 땅으로 [배를] 되돌리려고 힘껏 [노를] 저었으나, 할 수 없었다. 바다가 그들을 향하여 점점 더 거칠어졌기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그 사람들은 오히려 배를 육지로 되돌리려고 힘껏 노를 저었다. 그러나 그럴 수 없었다. 바다가 그들을 향해 점점 더 사나워졌기 때문이다.
ko.R: 선원들은 그 대신 배를 육지로 돌리려고 힘껏 노를 저었다. 그러나 그렇게 할 수 없었다. 폭풍이 점점 더 심해졌기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: dug: rowed hard
decisions.reason: The verb means to dig, and here pictures the oars digging into the water. The sailors try everything to save Jonah's life before doing what he asked.

decisions.choice: they could not: the LORD's purpose cannot be escaped
decisions.reason: Jonah fled toward the open sea; the sailors try to bring him back to dry land, and the sea will not let them. Only when the LORD's will is done does the sea grow calm (verse 15).

decisions.choice: [in their oars] (L); Instead (B, R); the ship (R)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words that make the picture clear (m1). Balanced and Readable say "rowed hard", and begin with "Instead" because the sailors do not at once do what Jonah said. Readable says "get the ship back".

decisions.choice: "cavaron [con los remos]" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew verb "dig" and brackets what it refers to, the oars, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: "ra sức chèo [mạnh]"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "dug" is the rowers' stroke; Vietnamese "chèo" already names the oars, so Literal brackets only the effort, not the oars the English brackets.

source.text: וַיִּקְרְא֨וּ אֶל־יְהוָ֜ה וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אָנָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אַל־נָ֣א נֹאבְדָ֗ה בְּנֶ֨פֶשׁ֙ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֔ה וְאַל־תִּתֵּ֥ן עָלֵ֖ינוּ דָּ֣ם נָקִ֑יא כִּֽי־אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר חָפַ֖צְתָּ עָשִֽׂיתָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they called to Yahweh and said, Please, Yahweh, do not, please, let us perish for [the] life of this man, and do not put on us innocent blood; for you, Yahweh, as you pleased you have done.

en.L: And they called to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do not let us perish for the life of this man, and do not lay on us innocent blood; for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have done as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} pleased."
en.B: Then they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do not let us perish for taking this man's life! Do not hold us guilty of innocent blood. For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have done as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} pleased."
en.R: Then the sailors prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}," they said, "do not let us die for taking this man's life. Do not hold us guilty of killing an innocent man. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wanted to do."

vi.L: Họ kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và nói: "Ôi, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin đừng để chúng con chết mất vì mạng sống của người này, và xin đừng đổ huyết vô tội trên chúng con; vì, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm theo điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn."
vi.B: Bấy giờ họ kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Ôi, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin đừng để chúng con chết mất vì lấy mạng sống người này! Xin đừng kể chúng con có tội làm đổ huyết vô tội. Vì, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn."
vi.R: Rồi các thủy thủ cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Ôi, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin đừng để chúng con phải chết vì lấy mạng người này. Xin đừng bắt tội chúng con giết một người vô tội. Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn làm."

es.L: Y clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y dijeron: «Te rogamos, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que no perezcamos por la vida de este hombre, y no pongas sobre nosotros sangre inocente; porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, has hecho como has querido».
es.B: Entonces clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «¡Por favor, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, no nos dejes perecer por quitarle la vida a este hombre! No nos culpes de sangre inocente. Porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, has hecho lo que has querido».
es.R: Entonces los marineros oraron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. «Por favor, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}», dijeron, «no nos dejes morir por quitarle la vida a este hombre. No nos culpes de matar a un hombre inocente. {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has hecho lo que querías hacer».

fr.L: Et ils crièrent vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et dirent : « De grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ne nous laisse pas périr à cause de la vie de cet homme, et ne mets pas sur nous un sang innocent ; car {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait comme il {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a plu. »
fr.B: Alors ils crièrent vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : « De grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ne nous fais pas périr pour avoir pris la vie de cet homme ! Ne nous rends pas coupables d’un sang innocent. Car {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as agi comme {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’as voulu. »
fr.R: Alors les marins ont prié {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : « De grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ne nous fais pas mourir parce que nous prenons la vie de cet homme. Ne nous rends pas coupables d’avoir tué un innocent. {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, c’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui as fait ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} voulais. »

sw.L: Ndipo wakamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakasema, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali, usituache tuangamie kwa ajili ya uhai wa mtu huyu, wala usitutwike damu isiyo na hatia; kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, umefanya kama ulivyopenda."
sw.B: Kisha wakamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali usituache tuangamie kwa sababu ya kuutoa uhai wa mtu huyu! Usituhesabie hatia ya damu isiyo na hatia. Kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, umefanya kama ulivyopenda."
sw.R: Kisha mabaharia wakamwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wakasema, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tafadhali usituache tufe kwa sababu ya kumwua mtu huyu. Usituhesabie hatia ya kumwua mtu asiye na hatia. Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umefanya yale uliyotaka kufanya."

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖어 말했다. "아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제발 이 사람의 목숨 때문에 저희가 망하지 않게 해 주십시오. 무죄한 피를 저희에게 돌리지 마십시오. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서는 기뻐하시는 대로 행하셨기 때문입니다."
ko.B: 그러자 그들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖었다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제발 이 사람의 목숨을 빼앗는다고 해서 저희를 망하게 하지 마십시오. 죄 없는 사람의 피를 흘린 죄를 저희에게 묻지 마십시오. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서는 뜻하신 대로 이 일을 하셨습니다."
ko.R: 그러자 선원들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 기도했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제발 이 사람을 죽게 한다고 해서 저희를 죽이지 마십시오. 죄 없는 사람을 죽였다고 저희에게 벌을 내리지 마십시오. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서는 원하시는 대로 이 일을 하셨습니다."

decisions.choice: they called to the LORD: the sailors now pray to Jonah's God by name
decisions.reason: In verse 5 each sailor cried to his own god. Now they pray to the LORD, using his name three times. The pagans pray to the LORD while his prophet has not prayed at all (he first prays in 2:2).

decisions.choice: for the life of this man ... innocent blood: do not punish us for his death
decisions.reason: The sailors fear that killing Jonah will make them guilty of murder, and that his life will be required of them (Genesis 9:5-6; Deuteronomy 21:8). They ask not to be held guilty of shedding the blood of a man who, as far as they know, has done them no wrong.

decisions.choice: you have done as you pleased: the storm and the lot are the LORD's doing
decisions.reason: The sailors say that they are acting on the LORD's will, shown by the storm and the lot, not their own. Compare Psalm 115:3: "whatever he pleases he does".

decisions.choice: Please, LORD, with no "O"; for taking this man's life (B, R); innocent man (R)
decisions.reason: The LORD addressed by name is "LORD" with no "O", as set for the prophets. Balanced and Readable say what "for the life of this man" means (m2). Readable says "an innocent man" for "innocent blood", and starts a new sentence with "LORD".

decisions.choice: vocative "SEÑOR" with no "oh"; the sailors say "tú" to God
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets for the sailors' prayer (1:14) and as published Spanish addresses God.

decisions.choice: "De grâce, SEIGNEUR" (the vocative divine-name span, with no article and no "ô"); God is "tu" with deity_pronoun spans on "toi", "tu", "t'"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets for the sailors' prayer and the Psalms for prayer to God.

decisions.choice: "Ôi, lạy CHÚA" and "chúng con"
decisions.reason: The terms note: the sailors praying to the LORD say "Ôi, lạy CHÚA" for the pleading "Please, LORD" and call themselves "chúng con", as worshippers do.

decisions.choice: "Ee BWANA, tafadhali"
decisions.reason: The sailors' prayer takes the vocative "Ee", as the published Psalms address the LORD, with the divine_name span on BWANA (term sheet).

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun span on the free pronoun "wewe" only
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb ("umefanya", "ulivyopenda"), and a verb prefix cannot take a capital, so a span goes only on a free pronoun or possessive. Jonah, Micah and Nahum therefore have fewer spans than the English. Noted once for these books.

decisions.choice: The sailors pray in 합쇼체 with "저희", calling on "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여" and saying "주님께서" for "you"
decisions.reason: Prayer is 합쇼체 in the published prophets and Psalms, with the vocative "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여" (no "O") [Ps 19:15]. Korean avoids a bare "you" to God and uses "주님", as Isaiah and Jeremiah do.

source.text: וַיִּשְׂאוּ֙ אֶת־יוֹנָ֔ה וַיְטִלֻ֖הוּ אֶל־הַיָּ֑ם וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד הַיָּ֖ם מִזַּעְפּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they picked up Jonah and hurled him into the sea, and stood the sea from its raging.

en.L: And they picked up Jonah and hurled him into the sea, and the sea stood still from its raging.
en.B: Then they picked Jonah up and hurled him into the sea, and the sea stopped its raging.
en.R: Then they picked Jonah up and threw him into the sea. And the sea became calm.

vi.L: Rồi họ nhấc Giô-na lên và ném ông xuống biển, thì biển ngừng cơn giận dữ.
vi.B: Rồi họ khiêng Giô-na lên và ném ông xuống biển, và biển liền ngưng cuồng nộ.
vi.R: Rồi họ khiêng Giô-na lên và quăng ông xuống biển. Biển liền lặng sóng.

es.L: Y tomaron a Jonás y lo lanzaron al mar, y el mar se detuvo de su furia.
es.B: Luego tomaron a Jonás y lo lanzaron al mar, y el mar dejó de rugir con furia.
es.R: Luego tomaron a Jonás y lo echaron al mar. Y el mar se calmó.

fr.L: Et ils prirent Jonas et le lancèrent dans la mer ; et la mer s’arrêta de sa fureur.
fr.B: Puis ils prirent Jonas et le lancèrent dans la mer, et la fureur de la mer cessa.
fr.R: Puis ils ont pris Jonas et ils l’ont jeté dans la mer. Et la mer est devenue calme.

sw.L: Wakamwinua Yona, wakamtupa baharini, nayo bahari ikasimama, ikaacha kuchafuka kwake.
sw.B: Kisha wakamwinua Yona, wakamtupa baharini, nayo bahari ikaacha kuchafuka.
sw.R: Kisha wakamwinua Yona, wakamtupa baharini. Bahari ikatulia.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 요나를 들어 바다에 내던지니, 바다가 그 사나움을 멈추고 섰다.
ko.B: 그들이 요나를 들어 바다에 내던지자, 사납게 날뛰던 바다가 멈추었다.
ko.R: 그들이 요나를 들어서 바다에 던졌다. 그러자 바다가 잔잔해졌다.

decisions.choice: the sea stopped raging: at once, showing that the storm was the LORD's
decisions.reason: The storm ends as soon as Jonah is in the sea. The sailors see that Jonah's words were true and that the LORD controls the sea, and their response follows in verse 16 (compare Mark 4:39-41, where the disciples see a storm stilled).

decisions.choice: hurled (L, B); threw (R); stood still from its raging (L); stopped its raging (B); became calm (R)
decisions.reason: The verb "hurl" comes for the last time, as in verse 4. Literal keeps the picture of the sea "standing", that is, standing still; Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

source.text: וַיִּֽירְא֧וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֛ים יִרְאָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּֽזְבְּחוּ־זֶ֨בַח֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וַֽיִּדְּר֖וּ נְדָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And feared the men a fear great Yahweh, and they sacrificed a sacrifice to Yahweh and vowed vows.

en.L: And the men feared {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [with] a great fear, and they sacrificed a sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and vowed vows.
en.B: Then the men were filled with great fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they offered a sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and made vows.
en.R: Then the sailors were filled with awe for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They offered a sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and made solemn promises to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

vi.L: Những người ấy kính sợ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [với] một nỗi sợ lớn, và họ dâng một sinh tế cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và khấn hứa những lời hứa nguyện.
vi.B: Bấy giờ những người ấy vô cùng kính sợ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Họ dâng sinh tế cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và khấn hứa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Bấy giờ các thủy thủ hết lòng kính sợ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Họ dâng một sinh tế cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và trịnh trọng hứa nguyện với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

es.L: Y temieron los hombres {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} [con] gran temor, y sacrificaron un sacrificio {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} e hicieron votos.
es.B: Entonces los hombres se llenaron de un gran temor {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y ofrecieron un sacrificio {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} e hicieron votos.
es.R: Entonces los marineros sintieron un profundo respeto por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Ofrecieron un sacrificio {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hicieron promesas solemnes.

fr.L: Et les hommes craignirent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [avec] une grande crainte, et ils sacrifièrent un sacrifice {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et firent des vœux.
fr.B: Alors ces hommes furent remplis d’une grande crainte envers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; ils offrirent un sacrifice {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et firent des vœux.
fr.R: Alors les marins ont été remplis de respect pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Ils ont offert un sacrifice {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont fait des promesses solennelles.

sw.L: Na watu wale wakamcha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa hofu kuu, wakamtolea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} dhabihu, wakaweka nadhiri.
sw.B: Ndipo watu wale wakajawa na hofu kuu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wakamtolea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} dhabihu, wakaweka nadhiri.
sw.R: Ndipo mabaharia wakajawa na hofu na heshima kuu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wakamtolea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} dhabihu, wakaweka ahadi nzito {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.

ko.L: 그러자 그 사람들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 큰 두려움으로 두려워하여, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 희생 제물을 바치고 서원들을 했다.
ko.B: 그러자 그 사람들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 크게 경외하게 되어, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 제물을 바치고 서원을 했다.
ko.R: 그러자 선원들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 깊이 경외하게 되었다. 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 제물을 바치고, 그분께 꼭 지키겠다고 약속을 했다.

decisions.choice: feared the LORD with a great fear: now the fear is awe and worship
decisions.reason: The third "great fear" of the chapter (verses 10 and 16, after verse 5) is now directed to the LORD himself. It is the fear that Jonah claimed in verse 9: reverence that leads to worship. The pagan sailors end the chapter worshiping the God their passenger fled.

decisions.choice: sacrificed and vowed: they worshiped the LORD and made promises to him
decisions.reason: A vow was a promise to give God something, often a further sacrifice, usually made in danger or in gratitude for rescue (Psalm 66:13-14; 116:18). The text does not say where they sacrificed, on board or after reaching land. Jonah too will promise sacrifice and vows (2:10).

decisions.choice: feared ... [with] a great fear (L); great fear of (B); filled with awe (R); made vows (B); made solemn promises (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew pattern. Readable says "awe" because the fear here is reverence, not terror (m1), and explains a vow as a solemn promise.

decisions.choice: "temieron ... [con] gran temor" (L); "se llenaron de un gran temor" (B); "sintieron un profundo respeto" (R); "hicieron votos" (L, B); "promesas solemnes" (R)
decisions.reason: The fear is now reverence for the LORD; Readable says so with "respeto", which in Spanish carries awe.

decisions.choice: "kính sợ" (reverent fear) here, against "sợ hãi" (terror) in 1:5 and 1:10
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says the fear has become awe and worship; Vietnamese has two words where the Hebrew has one, so "kính sợ" marks the turn, as in 1:9.

decisions.choice: "큰 두려움으로 두려워하여" (L); "크게 경외하게 되어" (B); "깊이 경외하게 되었다" (R)
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew phrase as 1:10, but now the fear is awe toward the LORD (meaning decision): Literal keeps the repeated word, Balanced and Readable change to "경외하다" as at 1:9 B.
